record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine the function m^ch_d giving, for each rank d, the minimum possible number of flags of a chiral d-polytope.

evidence.quote: Problem 35 Find the value of mchd as a function of d.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract d-polytope is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ with a least element $F_{-1}$ and a greatest element $F_d$, satisfying the following: every maximal chain (called a flag) has exactly $d+2$ elements, so each element has a well-defined rank in $\{-1,0,1,\dots,d\}$; $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected; and $\mathcal{P}$ satisfies the diamond condition (for every pair $F<G$ with $\mathrm{rank}(G)-\mathrm{rank}(F)=2$, there are exactly two elements $H$ with $F<H<G$). Two flags are called $i$-adjacent if they differ in exactly the rank-$i$ element. The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts freely on the set of flags.

The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called regular if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts transitively on flags. It is called chiral if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ has exactly two orbits on flags, with the property that adjacent flags always lie in different orbits.

For each integer $d\ge 3$, define
$$m^{\mathrm{ch}}_d \;=\; \min igl\{\,|\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{P})|\,:\, \mathcal{P}	ext{ is a chiral abstract }d	ext{-polytope} igr\},$$
where $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{P})$ denotes the set of flags of $\mathcal{P}$, and the minimum is taken over all finite chiral $d$-polytopes (set $m^{\mathrm{ch}}_d=\infty$ if no chiral $d$-polytope exists in rank $d$).

Determine the function $d\mapsto m^{\mathrm{ch}}_d$ for all $d\ge 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the minimum number of flags of a chiral d-polytope as a function of d appears to remain open in general. Partial results are known: lower bounds of the form 48(d-2)(d-2)! for sufficiently large d, results on tight chiral polytopes showing none exist for rank n ≥ 6, and explicit small examples in low ranks, but no closed-form determination of m^ch_d for all d has been established.

status_evidence.title: Tight chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Tight chiral polytopes are studied; results show non-existence of tight chiral n-polytopes for n ≥ 6.
status_evidence.claim: Partial information on minimum flag counts in chiral polytopes is known, but no complete formula.

status_evidence.title: Non-Flat Regular Polytopes and Restrictions on Chiral Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Restrictions are proved that yield lower bounds on the number of flags of chiral polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds are established but the exact minimum function remains undetermined.
